identity.name: link_wsib
identity.description: Matches WSIB registry entries to builder entities via a 3-tier bulk SQL cascade (exact trade name 0.95, exact legal name 0.90, pg_trgm fuzzy 0.60) and writes wsib_registry.linked_entity_id/match_confidence/matched_at plus entities.is_wsib_registered and the fill-only contact columns, per tier, in one step-scoped transaction.

why_lock.text: Lock 94 is not the spec number (this step's primary governing spec is 46). It was assigned by the c1ef0b73 advisory-lock retrofit and is recorded in src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts's registry ('scripts/link-wsib.js': 94) — kept textually per §5.4 so that registry stays green across the conversion.

guard_why.text: The compute-authored matched CTE (buildTierSql) folds `WHERE w.linked_entity_id IS NULL` into every tier's own predicate, so a row this UPDATE can reach is, by construction, currently NULL — the guard is genuinely enforced (write.js's set-based codegen now appends an IS DISTINCT FROM clause when declared, LG-11 sibling work) even though the scope predicate alone already makes a re-run a zero-write no-op.

write_discipline.scope: linked_entity_id IS NULL (folded into the per-tier matched CTE, not a separate outer WHERE — LG-11's whole reason to exist: the SET clause's values are per-row JOIN results, not a declared constant, so this target cannot use set_based_scoped's constant-only codegen)

why.text: LG-11 (finding 3, Fold A/B, 2026-08-28). Neither pre-existing write.js executor fits: executeSetBasedClear only writes a DECLARED CONSTANT; executeUpsertBatch is ALWAYS INSERT-capable (ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE), and wsib_registry rows may only ever be CREATED by load-wsib.js — an accidental INSERT here would violate that ownership boundary worse than a missed match. write.executeSetBasedJoinUpdate refuses any statement containing INSERT INTO or ON CONFLICT at execution time (checked on the actual SQL text, not a class label).

write_discipline.scope: id IN (SELECT linked_entity_id FROM wsib_registry WHERE match_confidence = $1) AND is_wsib_registered = false

why.text: G-9: runs immediately after EACH tier's own wsib_registry UPDATE, scoped to $1 = that tier's resolved confidence (write.executeSetBasedClear's existing scopeParams binding, no write.js change needed) — not deferred to a single end-of-run pass over all confidences.

guard_why.text: 647d0935's copyContacts NULLIF-guard, ported verbatim: only fills a currently-empty contact field, never overwrites (Spec 46 §2 Contact Flow, G-15). The set clause's right-hand sides are subquery-aggregated per entity, not a declared constant, so this target uses the same LG-11 executor as the wsib join-update rather than set_based_scoped's constant-only codegen.

write_discipline.scope: w_agg.linked_entity_id = e.id AND wsib_registry.match_confidence = $1, aggregated per tier (fill-only via NULLIF, never overwrite)

why.text: Once a contact field is filled, the NULLIF(...) IS NULL guard excludes the row from ever matching again — a re-run over an unchanged corpus changes 0 rows, same idempotence class as the wsib_registry join-update.

guard_why.text: Only touches a row currently non-NULL (a repeat mode-full run over an already-retracted set changes 0 rows) — genuinely enforced by write.js's set-based guard-clause codegen (LG-11 sibling growth), not merely by the scope predicate alone.

idempotent_rerun_why.text: A genuine repair MOVES rows by design (that is the point of A-7) — zero_writes would be a false declaration on the one invocation this target exists for. The step-level idempotence claim lives on the wsib join-update target (writes[0]), which this target's own guard keeps from re-touching an already-retracted row.

declared_drift.text: Rows retracted per FULL invocation = wsib_registry rows currently linked_entity_id IS NOT NULL AND match_confidence = the tier-3 confidence value — measured 13,645 total tier-3 links (8,450 of them, 61.9%, failing today's d704a447 predicate; LW-D5). Bounded by the table's tier-3 population, never by the whole table.

why.text: LG-16 (Fold B, Cross-read Adversary, A-7 mechanism amendment). write.js's only pre-existing retraction primitive is executeRetraction — a DELETE, safe for link_massing's wholly-owned parcel_buildings junction but UNSAFE here: wsib_registry ROWS are load-wsib.js's exclusive territory, and retracting a LINK must never retract the ROW. Codegen-identical to set_based_scoped/unscoped (a constant SET — always null — over a declared scope) but declared under its OWN class so a reviewer can find every place this step ever retracts by grepping the class name, and so the LG-16 fence lock can assert 'never DELETE' against the generated SQL rather than against a scope string.

invalidates.when: a wsib_registry row links to this entity for the first time (any tier), or A-7's tier-3 repair retracts the entity's only remaining link — enrich-web-search.js's last_enriched_at IS NULL gate is the plan's identified consumer (Cross-Layer Contract 1); whether that gate genuinely needs re-invalidation on THIS column is an open Ask this pilot does not resolve, filed to review_followups.

why.text: Steady-state (incremental mode): 3 tiers x 3 statements (wsib join-update, entities flag, entities contacts) = 9 statement executions / 7 distinct SQL texts (the flag statement's shape repeats identically across tiers with only its $1 binding changing) / 3 write groups on 2 tables (Fold A, Integration S1, 2026-08-28). The mode-full-only LG-16 retraction + its entities-unflag cascade + its copyContacts reverse pass add 3 MORE statement executions, but ONLY when mode resolves full — not counted in this steady-state inventory, and not exercised by this commit (A-8: mode never resolves full absent a genuine corpus/FORCE_FULL signal).

on_prior_run_error_why.text: A failed prior-run read degrades this step to 'no baseline' — the config_version diff and the upstream_ledger count both fail-safe to CHANGED (never SKIP) on an absent baseline, so warn_row's cost is a real run rather than a silently stale gate, unlike an ingest loader whose baseline gates a destructive departure DELETE.

why.text: Tier 3's entire predicate is pg_trgm similarity() over GIN trigram indexes (measured live: v1.6, present). Without it the fuzzy tier cannot run at all — there is no second algorithm to fall back to (unlike link_massing's now-retired JS path).

The GIN trigram index Tier 3's trade_name_normalized comparison seeks. Without it the % operator degrades to a sequential scan over 121,116 rows per batch — the same class of failure tasks/lessons.md records for link_massing's spatial GiST indexes.
The GIN trigram index for legal_name_normalized — the other half of Tier 3's UNION ALL split (647d0935, avoiding the ~394M-row nested loop the OR-joined version produced).
Measured live: relrowsecurity=true, 0 policies. Under any role that does not bypass RLS every tier's UPDATE affects 0 rows with NO error — indistinguishable from an unchanged corpus.
Same class, the other side of the join: entities also carries RLS enabled.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a value the library already measured — a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition. It must redden the run, not drop its row.

expect.reports: the resolved mode and the ledger gated-skip decision

why.text: LG-15's gated-skip and A-8's tri-state mode, on the record — visible even on a gated skip (the same class as link_massing's full_mode_gate row).
LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL left standing bypasses the ledger gate on every subsequent run. Reported (not gated) so a forgotten override is discoverable by reading the audit table.

D-20-class guard for A-7's LG-16 repair: against an empty entities corpus, a mode-full run would retract every tier-3 link and repair nothing. Scored pre_write — before the retraction statement — so an unaccepted FAIL means no statement is issued. Never fires in incremental mode (entities measured 3,948, never 0).

expect.of: cumulative linked / total wsib_registry rows, all tiers, all time

why.text: LW-D1, the P4 violation this pilot closes: pre-conversion the floor was the bare literal 5 in `linkRate >= 5 ? PASS : WARN`. Reported as the RATE itself (not the unlinked complement, unlike link_massing's link_rate — T2's config value IS the floor, so a `pct >=` form is the correctly-shaped comparison; `pct <=` would compare the wrong direction). Cumulative, never run-scoped, for the same reason link_massing's link_rate is cumulative. Measured cumulative rate 11.53% (contaminated) / clean rate 4.55% (below floor, A-7's whole reason to exist). R-H (Spec 124 Rule 10 addendum): a standing non-zero population is WARN with a declared, machine-observable retighten condition, never FAIL, never INFO-by-taste — link_wsib got this right before R-H was ratified (R-F item 3, confirmed not fixed this pilot). RETIGHTEN CONDITION: once A-7's tier-3 repair (LG-16, commit 8's budgeted FULL) converges (`tier3_full_not_converged` reads clean and `wsib_tier3_current_predicate_pass_rate_pct` reads 100), the clean and cumulative rates collapse to the same number — at that point `link_wsib_link_rate_warn_pct` should be reviewed for raising above its current 5, since the 4.55%-vs-11.53% contamination gap this floor was set against will have closed.

expect.of: the max wsib_registry rows linked to any single entity

why.text: T6, new this pilot (Fold A, Reality-Check). Fires immediately on the known-bad population (171 magnet entities fan-in >= 10, worst MDK CONSTRUCTION at 2,118) — intended, not a defect (Fold B ACCEPTED ruling). A declared, machine-observable population this pilot surfaces rather than gates away. R-H (Spec 124 Rule 10 addendum): WARN with a declared, machine-observable retighten condition, never FAIL, never INFO-by-taste. RETIGHTEN CONDITION: the fan-in magnets are near-entirely tier-3 (fuzzy, 0.60-confidence) contamination — once A-7's tier-3 repair (LG-16) retracts the 61.9%-failing tier-3 links, `wsib_entity_fanin_max` should fall well below its current 2,118 (MDK CONSTRUCTION) and 1,404 (COLE CONTRACTING); at that point `link_wsib_entity_fanin_warn` (currently 20, deliberately loose so the check fires on the known-bad population rather than gating it away) should be reviewed for lowering toward a tighter bound that reflects genuinely healthy fan-in.
Invariant, pinned by the golden captures (commit 5): a linked_entity_id with a NULL match_confidence or matched_at is a partial write the cascade's own paired columns should make impossible.
The written vocabulary is the three resolved tier confidences (T3/T4/T5) — no other value should ever reach the column.

why.text: LW-D4, INCIDENTAL classification (PH-6): no code path ever writes a confidence in this range, so the pre-conversion stats query's 0.50 lower bound was always dead. Reported, not fixed — a declared limitation, not a defect.

Invariant, pinned by the golden captures. is_wsib_registered may only be true because a wsib_registry row links to this entity — a registered entity with zero links is the write ORDER breaking (G-9), or A-7's unflag cascade missing a row.

T7 / A-7 convergence (Fold B, BLOCKING b). TIER3_SELECT is capped LIMIT 1000/invocation; a single mode-full pass repairs at most 1,000 of ~5,515 clean rows. Bounded by link_wsib_tier3_full_max_iterations (T7, default 20, read via tiers[].max_iterations_from_config — LW-D10, commit 8b); exhaustion is WARN, never FAIL, per R-H (a standing non-convergence is a real operational condition to see, not a reason to redden the run). RETIGHTEN CONDITION: if this WARN fires on a live repair, the FIRST response is to re-run the repair (LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL=1) before considering T7's default too low — 20 iterations against a ~1,000-row-per-pass cap already covers ~20,000 candidate rows, well above any single tier-3 population measured to date (13,645). Only raise T7's default if a repeat exhaustion is measured against an unchanged corpus.

why.text: Fold B BLOCKING a. Measured local exposure is 0 (PH-6: wsib_registry carries zero contact values on this DB, so copyContacts has copied nothing, ever, locally) — a limitations[] entry records this does NOT bound cloud.

expect.writable: the role bypasses RLS, or a policy grants the write

why.text: Reports the MEASURED privilege on every run, not only the failing one — the guards.requires precondition's evidence.

The schema's own drafters GUESSED a re-derivation from the OLD fused evidence-base labels without measuring. Measured this pilot (Fold A, Integration S1 + LG-11/LG-16 findings): the wsib_registry write is NOT expressible as class E (write_once_backfill) or G (set_based_scoped) — the SET clause's values are per-row JOIN results from a compute-authored matched CTE, which neither pre-existing class's codegen can generate. The correct classes are the two NEW ones this pilot adds: set_based_join_update (LG-11) and set_based_null_retract (LG-16). Spec 122 §1.4's text is stale and is corrected in the same commit (Spec Update step).

deviations.from: the pre-conversion hand-rolled B3 run-ledger gate (OWN_SLUGS/UPSTREAM_SLUGS arrays in scripts/link-wsib.js)

why.text: LG-15. Generalized into staleness.ledgerGatedSkip + deriveLedgerSlugs (scripts/lib/step/staleness.js), which derives own/upstream slugs from inputs.reads.steps[] + execution.invocation rather than a hand-maintained array — one of the four hand-maintained spellings in the pre-conversion file was already refuted in-file (the 'entities' chain claim, v5:60).

deviations.from: Spec 60 §Step Registry's write-target declaration ('entities' only) and its method description ('Levenshtein distance')

why.text: G-16/G-17, both measured CONFLICTS with the spec's own text (not behavior changes): the step also writes wsib_registry (G-16), and the real method is pg_trgm trigram similarity in a 3-tier exact/exact/fuzzy cascade, never Levenshtein (G-17). Both corrected in the same commit (Spec Update step) — the code was already right, only the spec prose was stale.

deviations.adjudicated_by: measured this pilot (§1 PH-0, boundary freeze), 2026-08-28

deviations.from: Spec 122 §1.2 checks[].limit's closed form set (pct <= only)

why.text: A genuine library gap, closed per Spec 124 §7 rung (d): link_wsib's link_rate_warn is a config-driven PERCENTAGE FLOOR (T2 = the floor value itself, not its complement — unlike link_massing's link_rate, where the config value coincidentally equals its own complement). limit_from_config's substitution is unconditional, so no existing form (pct <=, viol <=/==, pop >=) could express 'value >= the substituted config number' for a percentage. scripts/lib/step/verdict.js gains a symmetric pct >= form (evaluateLimit, PCT_RE) — every future step with a floor-shaped percentage check benefits, not just this one.

limitations.what: staleness.fingerprint_inputs' wsib_registry corpus signal is COUNT(*) only (upstream_ledger). G-19's fuller reading — trade_name_normalized is rewritten on EVERY load_wsib reload even when linked_entity_id is untouched, so an unchanged row count can still sit on a stale matching predicate — is not captured by a row-count-only signal. A MAX(last_seen_at)-based signal, or reading load_wsib's own source-version fingerprint directly, would close this; not built this commit.
limitations.measured: load-wsib.js ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET rewrites trade_name_normalized/last_seen_at on every reload but never linked_entity_id/match_confidence/matched_at (Fold C, confirmed by direct read, 2026-08-28)

limitations.what: A-7's copyContacts reverse-clear pass is provenance-by-equality: an entity's contact field is cleared only when its CURRENT value equals a value that existed on a now-retracted wsib row. A contact that coincidentally matches a retracted row's value is cleared and re-copied on relink (a false positive, not a false negative — no contact is ever left dangling from a genuinely retracted source).
limitations.measured: magnet_entities_with_any_contact = 7 of 171 magnets, but wsib_registry carries ZERO contact values locally (121,116 / 0 / 0) — the local 0 exposure does NOT bound cloud, which may carry Serper-enriched wsib_registry contact fields; re-run both queries against cloud before any cloud FULL run (PH-6, commit 4)

limitations.what: The [0.50, 0.60) match_confidence stats bucket boundary (a display-only artifact of the pre-conversion final-stats query) is DEAD — no code path writes a confidence in that range, since the three tiers write exactly 0.95/0.90/0.60. PINNED (Spec 123 §3.1), not fixed: nothing downstream reads or asserts on the boundary specifically.
limitations.measured: 0 rows with match_confidence in [0.50, 0.60) (golden capture invariant wsib_dead_bucket_050_060_count = 0, commit 5)

recovery.reset: TRUNCATE is never correct for wsib_registry (load-wsib.js owns row lifecycle) or entities. Re-run with LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL=1, which bypasses the ledger gate; the tier-3 repair itself is gated separately by mode resolving full (A-8's corpus signal, never schedule).

why.text: The normal outcome: the ledger gate did not skip, mode resolved incremental, the cascade ran.
Mode resolved full (A-8's corpus signal or LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL): LG-16's tier-3 repair ran. NOT reachable by any commit-7 invocation — commit 8's budgeted act.
A WARN row stands (link_rate_warn, entity_fanin_warn, or tier3_full_not_converged) and nothing FAILED. The run completed and wrote; the warning is in the table.

LG-15: no upstream wsib_registry/entities activity and no config_version bump since link_wsib's own last completed run — generalizes the pre-existing B3 SKIP. Re-emits the prior run's threshold_updated_at so the NEXT run's config_version diff still has a baseline.
G-12: unlinked_start measured 0 — every wsib_registry row already carries a link. A genuine zero-work completion, distinct from a gated skip (the step ran and measured; nothing was eligible).
Advisory lock 94 is held by another process — a row-derived SKIP summary, never a bare SDK skip with no audit_table.
Mode resolved full against an empty entities corpus — the pre_write refusal, no retraction statement issued.
RLS enabled with 0 policies and the role does not bypass — every statement would affect 0 rows with no error.
A guards.requires precondition with on_missing: "fail" is absent (pg_trgm, a trigram index, or an RLS policy). Refuses before reading anything.

A declared logic variable (T1-T7) resolved outside its bounds under on_invalid: "fail". hoisted_above_gate puts this refusal ABOVE the advisory lock and the ledger gate — the opposite of the pre-conversion order (Commit A / A1 fix).
